# Detected NHST Results and Consistency

::: {.section-card}

The table below shows the `statcheck` results for your manuscript. Each row represents a reported Null Hypothesis Significance Test (NHST), with the original and recomputed p-values. The **Status** column uses colored bullets to indicate consistency:

* **Green** = consistent  
* **Yellow** = inconsistent but does not affect significance  
* **Red** = inconsistent and affects significance at the .05 level  

```{r}
# Load the statcheck output
stat <- params$statcheckOutput

# Classify Consistency as a simple factor/character
stat$Consistency <- ifelse(
  stat$decision_error,
  "Decision Inconsistency",
  ifelse(stat$error, "Inconsistency", "Consistent")
)

# Round computed p-value to 6 decimals to improve legibility
format_number <- function(x, digits = 6, sci_cut = 1e-6) {
  ifelse(
    abs(x) < sci_cut & x != 0,
    formatC(x, digits = digits, format = "e"),
    formatC(x, digits = digits, format = "f")
  )
}

stat$computed_p <- format_number(stat$computed_p)

# Subset columns and rename
stat_sparse <- stat[c("source", "raw", "computed_p", "Consistency")]
colnames(stat_sparse) <- c("Article", "Result As Given In Text", "Computed P-Value", "Consistency")

# Assign colored bullets
red    <- "<span style='color:red; font-size: 20pt;'>&#9679;</span>"
yellow <- "<span style='color:orange; font-size: 20pt;'>&#9679;</span>"
green  <- "<span style='color:green; font-size: 20pt;'>&#9679;</span>"

Status <- ifelse(
  stat_sparse$Consistency == "Decision Inconsistency", red,
  ifelse(stat_sparse$Consistency == "Inconsistency", yellow, green)
)

# Optionally make the text bold for inconsistencies
stat_sparse$Consistency <- ifelse(
  stat_sparse$Consistency %in% c("Inconsistency", "Decision Inconsistency"),
  paste0("<b>", stat_sparse$Consistency, "</b>"),
  stat_sparse$Consistency
)

# Add Code column
stat_sparse <- cbind(stat_sparse, Status)

# Render interactive table
datatable(
  stat_sparse,
  escape = FALSE,
  rownames = FALSE,
  options = list(
    pageLength = 10,
    autoWidth = TRUE,
    searching = TRUE,
    ordering = TRUE
  )
)
```
:::

## Table Interpretation

::: {.section-card}

| Variable               | Description                                                                                     |
|------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Article                | Name of the file that was checked                                                               |
| Result As Given In Text | Original statistical result extracted from the manuscript                                       |
| Computed P-Value       | P-value recomputed from the test statistic and degrees of freedom                                |
| Consistency            | Classification of the result (Consistent, Inconsistency, Decision Inconsistency)               |
| Status                 | Colored bullet indicating the result’s consistency: Green = Consistent, Yellow = Inconsistency, Red = Decision Inconsistency |

:::

## Important Notes

::: {.section-card}

- `statcheck` is automated and may **miss, misread, or misclassify** results.  
- Inconsistencies can result from errors in p-values, test statistics, degrees of freedom, or combinations of these.  
- `statcheck` computes **two-tailed p-values by default**. One-tailed p-values may appear as inconsistencies; the tool can adjust for one-tailed tests, but this report cannot determine whether one-tailed detection was enabled.  
- Some inconsistencies may be **intentional**, e.g., adjusted p-values or corrections like Bonferroni.  

> **Warning:** Do not make decisions about a manuscript based solely on a `statcheck` report.  

For more information on what `statcheck` can and cannot do, see the FAQ at <https://statcheck.io>.

:::
